clue.text: Film director (not Hill) taking a trip on the Thames with Age Concern?

definitions.note: Age Concern was a British charity for older people; here it is read as worry about getting older

indicators.note: a trip is a stumble or a jaunt, so the remaining letters go wandering into a new order
inside the brackets, not means the following word is to be dropped from the words before it

parts.note: taken as written: these two words supply the letters to work on
a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
the Isis is the name given to the Thames as it flows through Oxford

explanation.surface: A film-maker goes on a boat trip down the Thames in aid of an elderly people's charity.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove TOR from FILM DIRECTOR and rearrange the rest, then add ISIS. Age Concern was a British charity for older people.
explanation.definitionFit: A midlife crisis is the anxiety some people feel on reaching middle years, a worry literally about age; the question mark flags the pun.

clue.text: Explain why the Italian team's ready in Paris

parts.note: Inter Milan is the football club usually just called Inter
pret is French for ready

explanation.surface: Someone asks for an explanation of why an Italian football side is said to be prepared in Paris.
explanation.definitionFit: To interpret something is to make its meaning clear, a close synonym of the verb in the clue.

clue.text: Sweet money

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lollipop or ice ..., a confection on a stick
second meaning: British slang for cash

explanation.walkthrough: In British English a lolly is both a sweet on a stick and slang for money.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a sugary treat on a stick and is also informal British slang for cash.

clue.text: Very severely overweight friend

parts.note: fat means carrying too much weight
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A description of a companion who is dangerously heavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done fatally, such as being wounded, is done to the gravest possible degree, ending in death.

clue.text: Reinstate half the Conservatives? God!

parts.note: read as RE in state: RE placed inside CA, the abbreviation for the state of California

indicators.note: only half of the word survives, so its last three letters are dropped

parts.note: the Tories are Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims in disbelief at a plan to bring back half the Tory party.
explanation.walkthrough: Split Reinstate as RE in state, with CA (California) as the state. Tories is the nickname for Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: God is called the Creator as the maker of the universe, so the title stands for the deity.

clue.text: One book, with curious lilac cover, is senseless

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the jumbled lilac goes round the book, covering it
curious suggests something odd, so the letters of lilac are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled
a log is a book of records, such as a ship's log

explanation.surface: A single volume in an odd lilac jacket turns out to be nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illogical lacks reason or sense, so senseless is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Start to score at the crease — then test opener's run out

parts.note: in cricket a batsman at the crease is in, currently batting

indicators.note: the opener of a word is its first letter, as an opening batsman goes first

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken, the first ball of a Test match as it were
RO is the scorecard abbreviation for run out

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: a batsman gets off the mark in a Test match, then the opener is run out.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all cricket, but 'score' belongs to the definition: the opening of a musical score.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a piece of music, the beginning of a score.

clue.text: Order to fight leads to disorder in the ranks?

parts.note: a class is an order or category, as in biological classification
to struggle is to fight or wrestle

explanation.surface: A command to start fighting provokes chaos among the soldiers.
explanation.walkthrough: The ranks are not military but social classes, whose conflict is the disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: Class struggle is conflict between social strata, a punning kind of disorder among society's ranks.

clue.text: Exorcised man's about to be interrogated

indicators.note: about signals that these letters are turned around into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A man who has had a demon driven out of him is about to be questioned.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'S of man's is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be cross-examined is to be questioned closely, as a witness is in court.

clue.text: Appendage is small and utter drag

parts.note: little means small

indicators.note: utter means to speak, so we want a word pronounced like the one meaning drag

parts.note: to tow is to drag or haul

explanation.surface: Something tacked on is said to be both tiny and completely boring.
explanation.walkthrough: Utter looks like an adjective (complete), but it is a verb, to say.
explanation.definitionFit: The smallest digit of the foot is an extremity attached to the body, an appendage.

clue.text: Subsequent consumer sale returns one disregarded

indicators.note: the letter for one is ignored, so it is taken out
returns means the word for consumer sale is written backwards

parts.note: retail is selling goods to the consumer

explanation.surface: In a later season, shop sales come back, with one item overlooked.
explanation.definitionFit: Later and subsequent both mean coming afterwards in time.

clue.text: Foundling an artist depicted in a hovel

indicators.note: the artist is shown inside the hovel, as if painted within it

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty, and figuratively any filthy dwelling
RA, Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A painter portrays an abandoned child living in a squalid shack.
explanation.definitionFit: A stray is a homeless, abandoned creature, as a foundling is a deserted child.

clue.text: Drunk soldier on return promises to be keen to see action

parts.note: lit is slang for drunk

indicators.note: the soldier comes back, so his letters read backwards

parts.note: GI, an American soldier
IOUs are written promises to pay

explanation.surface: A tipsy serviceman back from duty makes vows and wants to get into a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Action is legal action, not combat.
explanation.definitionFit: A litigious person is eager to sue, keen to bring a lawsuit, which is legal action.

clue.text: They say sound of lion's in sync, maybe, but a bit thin

indicators.note: the sound-alike sits inside the other letters
maybe hints the letters of sync are only one possible order, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled

indicators.note: they say means we want a word that is pronounced like roar, in a non-rhotic accent

parts.note: a lion's sound is a roar

explanation.surface: A lion's roar is said to be in time with something, yet sounds a little weak.
explanation.walkthrough: In British pronunciation 'roar' and 'raw' sound the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrawny describes someone lean and bony, rather too thin.

clue.text: Toned down hanky-panky for women!

definitions.note: plural noun for a collective singular phrase meaning women as a group

parts.note: toned down means made weaker
a jokey word for sexual activity

explanation.surface: A milder version of naughty behaviour aimed at a female audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The exclamation mark flags an old-fashioned, now offensive phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The weaker sex is a dated, condescending idiom for females collectively.

clue.text: Lie about Charlie found with some cocaine?

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Charlie is C in the radio alphabet
a line is a single dose of powdered cocaine

explanation.surface: A lie told about a man named Charlie caught with drugs; Charlie is also slang for cocaine.
explanation.definitionFit: To recline is to lie back or rest in a horizontal position.

clue.text: There's no motion to maintain disunited Spain

definitions.note: a clause standing for an adjective meaning lifeless

indicators.note: disunited means broken apart, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

explanation.surface: A debating society notes that no motion has been put forward to keep a divided Spain together.
explanation.walkthrough: Motion looks like a debating proposal but means movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something inanimate is lifeless and does not move of its own accord.

clue.text: Mark left after Gunners' hectic routine

indicators.note: the mark comes after the gunners

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery
a trace is a mark left behind

explanation.surface: A football report: Arsenal, the Gunners, show a frantic pattern of play after a mark is made.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gunners is Arsenal's nickname, but here it is the Royal Artillery.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is an idiom for the relentless, competitive grind of working life.

clue.text: Licence included to rent it leasehold

definitions.note: noun form used for the verb meaning to give a right to

indicators.note: the answer is included within the following words

parts.note: the words that contain the answer, running across the word breaks

explanation.surface: A legal note: a licence is part of the deal to let a property on a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: To entitle someone is to give them the right or permission to do something, as licensing does.

clue.text: Letters in reply insult an Arab leader and his wife?

indicators.note: the answer is spelt out by letters in the following words

parts.note: the words that contain the answer, running across the word break

explanation.surface: A reply to a letter rudely insults an Arab ruler and his spouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arab leader is a sultan, and his wife is a sultana.
explanation.definitionFit: A sultana is the consort of a sultan, the ruler mentioned in the clue.

clue.text: Pianos are heard playing with singers

indicators.note: the letters are in play, moved about

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled

indicators.note: heard means we take the sound of the word, not its spelling

parts.note: the word are is pronounced exactly like the name of a letter

explanation.surface: Pianos can be heard being played to accompany a choir.
explanation.definitionFit: Soprani is the Italian plural of soprano, singers with the highest voice.

clue.text: March sees primroses opening and go to ruin

indicators.note: the letters are ruined, broken up and rebuilt in another order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the word whose first letter is taken
taken as written

explanation.surface: The month of March brings the first primroses, which then wither.
explanation.walkthrough: March looks like the month but is the verb to march.
explanation.definitionFit: The goose step is a stiff-legged way of marching, so as a verb it means to march.

clue.text: Regularly ring for daily directions

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
the FT, the Financial Times newspaper
E and N, the compass points east and north

explanation.surface: Someone frequently phones their cleaner, a daily, for instructions.
explanation.walkthrough: A daily is also British for a cleaner who comes in each day.
explanation.definitionFit: Often and regularly both describe something happening many times or frequently.

clue.text: Former heavyweight Bomber's single defence

parts.note: Muhammad Ali, former world heavyweight boxing champion
B is the designation for bomber aircraft, as in B-52
I, the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A retired boxer called Bomber mounts a solitary defence of his title.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of having been elsewhere, offered as a legal defence.

clue.text: Top clergyman's serious transgression

indicators.note: the top of the word, its first letter, is removed

parts.note: a parson is a clergyman

explanation.surface: A senior churchman has committed a grave sin.
explanation.walkthrough: Top looks like an adjective (senior), but it means behead.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a grave crime.

clue.text: Lily's destiny is with you and me

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate
us

explanation.surface: A woman called Lily declares her fate is bound up with ours.
explanation.definitionFit: The lotus is a water lily, sacred in Asian religions.

clue.text: Decipher language of drunken, lean tarts

indicators.note: drunken implies staggering about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Trying to make sense of the slurred speech of some skinny, tipsy women.
explanation.definitionFit: To translate is to render a text in another language, working out its meaning.

clue.text: Popular event to Germany's young?

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
an experience is an event lived through
D is the international vehicle code for Germany (Deutschland)

explanation.surface: A trendy event is held for German youth.
explanation.definitionFit: The young lack worldly knowledge, so they are by example green, unskilled and new to life.
